## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag ignores the `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, so it breaks the project's CLI-flag rule. That rule exists because CI sets options through the environment. The exclusion logic itself matches basenames as the docs describe, and the added tests cover it.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` uses `fnmatch` to skip any file whose basename matches one of the patterns, and `main` passes the flag's values to it. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for parsing, collection and archive contents, and adds a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Take the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Running with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` and no `--exclude` still archives `.log` files, because the flag uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so excluded files still end up in the archive. — Fix: Set the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, split into a list in a format you choose and document in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with a case where the variable is set.
